subject: PII handling, residency & emergency access — recap and asks
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.ram@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finedge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PII handling, residency & emergency access — recap and asks

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and three concrete asks so your security team can evaluate fit: 

1) Scope of PII: you confirmed the product will send account metadata + end-user email hashes and billing identifiers into Redwood for inference. Please confirm there is no raw SSN or full credit card numbers in the payloads.

2) Retention & logs: you said you need token-level request logs retained for 12 months for auditability and to support chargebacks; you also asked whether we can reduce retention to 90 days for non-billing logs. Our standard hosted offering keeps full request logs 365 days by default; we can propose a 90/365 split (redacted logs vs. full) depending on contract.

3) Support access / emergency break-glass: we discussed role-based support with tiered break-glass (support engineer, support manager, security reviewer). You asked for an auditable process that requires a required two-person approval for any privileged session and a time-limited elevation window.

Next steps (what I need from you):
- Confirm "no raw SSN/CCNs" in traffic (yes/no) and list any additional PII classes.
- Which retention model do you prefer (90/365 split or full 365)?
- Please share any existing playbooks for emergency access or a template SOC/incident policy if you want us to map controls.

Attached the security questionnaire we filled out during the call and a short draft playbook for support access for your comments.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up with Rishi (security) and Monica (solutions) next week.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: security-questionnaire-sorted.xlsx (spreadsheet), support-access-playbook.pdf (doc)

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finedge.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.ram@redwood.ai>
Cc: legalops@finedge.com
Date: 2027-06-05T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PII handling, residency & emergency access — recap and asks

Thanks Aisha — useful summary. Quick answers in-line: 

> Confirm "no raw SSN/CCNs" in traffic (yes/no) and list any additional PII classes.

No raw SSNs or full CCNs — confirmed. We do have postal addresses and DOB in some profiles; we can scope those out if needed.

> Which retention model do you prefer (90/365 split or full 365)?

For compliance, we need full 365 for billing reconciliation, but we could accept redacted request bodies after 90 days for troubleshooting logs.

> Please share any existing playbooks for emergency access or a template SOC/incident policy if you want us to map controls.

Looping in legalops for the playbook. We have an internal emergency access flow (PDF) — attaching to the thread. A few questions from our side:
- Can Redwood’s break-glass require two internal FinEdge approvers for an elevation to occur?
- Can we get per-session export of the decrypted payload and an audit transcript for each emergency access instance?

Sofia
Director, Security & Privacy
FinEdge Inc

Attachments: finedge-emergency-access.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finedge.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.ram@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PII handling, residency & emergency access — recap and asks

Sofia — Rishi from Security here, thanks for the details. A few technical confirmations and proposals: 

- Break-glass process: we can implement a two-party approval where one approver is a FinEdge admin and the second is an assigned FinEdge security reviewer (your choice), with Redwood requiring a one-time approval token from FinEdge to unlock session. We will record: approver identities, approval timestamps, session start/end, commands executed, and a transcript.

- Per-session export: we can provide an encrypted export bundle that contains the exact request payloads accessed during the session, plus an audit transcript. Exports are S3-compatible, signed, and can be pushed to your tenancy or to a secure transfer URL.

- RBAC model: we support role templates (viewer, support-readonly, support-privileged, admin). For support we recommend support-privileged which enforces MFA, IP allowlist, and time-limited elevation windows (max 4 hours) with automatic revocation.

- Data residency: your production data will be pinned to the US region as requested. For EU-only customers we offer region locking and separate tenancy; for your case we will confirm the hosting region and documentation in the contract.

I'll draft an appendix to the SOW describing break-glass flow and the per-session export mechanism for legalops to review.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

> On Jun 5, 2027, at 09:12, Aisha Rahman wrote:
> > Attached the security questionnaire we filled out during the call and a short draft playbook for support access for your comments.

From: legalops@finedge.com
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.ram@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PII handling, residency & emergency access — recap and asks

Hi team — Legal Ops here. Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of contract-level asks before we proceed to SOW: 

1) Data processing addendum (DPA): we need a DPA that specifies data categories, subprocessor list, deletion controls, and our requested 365-day logging retention for billing. Please provide a DPA draft.

2) Evidence for audit: can you provide sample audit logs (anonymized) and the SOC 2 control matrix mapping to your support access controls? We need both for our cloud security review board.

3) SLA & credits: if a break-glass mechanism fails and access can't be granted within the emergency window, what are the remedies? Please include proposed SLAs or credit language.

We appreciate the per-session export offer — please include export encryption and key custody details in the DPA or appendices.

If you can share the DPA and a short appendix for the break-glass flow by EOD Monday (2027-06-09), we can advance to legal review and a signature track.

Thanks,
FinEdge Legal Ops
legalops@finedge.com

--
Requested items: anonymized audit sample, DPA draft, SOC2 control matrix mapping, SLA language.
